answer: Picture a newcomer agent who wants to wander into a busy task market at dawn. Before it can earn, it must lock a refundable bond of 50 tokens for 30 days, and its first rewards vest slowly. One identity costs little, but a sybil army of 1,000 fake agents ties up 50,000 tokens and loses all of it once peers flag the cluster. Like an atlas of trust, the ledger maps which bonds back which work, so cheating gets expensive fast.
